evidence_note: Extracted directly from William Lilly's Christian Astrology (London 1647, first edition), the governing English witness of the Latin-European horary/natal tradition, via two independent public-domain archive.org witnesses of the 1647 printing: the Wellcome Collection scan b30338724 (Public Domain Mark; OCR text layer pinned as sources/ca1647_wellcome_djvu.txt sha256 7c08b55359c41049c5d43901b8da869a326f8eb852e4a30603a4b698533626aa) and the British Library microfilm scan bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_christian-astrology-_lilly-william_1647 (OCR pinned as sources/ca1647_bim_djvu.txt sha256 f661a0a140950cc53be09a8400ba87578f35b74b8724818b9f356cf6dd155e4d). Christian Astrology was checked against the EEBO-TCP catalog (textcreationpartnership/Texts TCP.csv) and is NOT among the TCP transcriptions, so OCR witnesses are the best available machine text; both were probed and found legible for connected prose (early-modern spelling and long-s preserved in the BIM layer), while the two load-bearing numeric tables (the p.107 orb table and the p.115 fortitude/debility point table) are OCR-degraded in both layers and were therefore read digit-by-digit from pinned photographs of the 1647 pages (sources/ca1647_wellcome_leaf141_p107_orb_table.jpg sha256 5d752cfce2dae1f287f8b646f988ee7dd77d2456388c5d73c95c5d3302ec8090 and sources/ca1647_wellcome_leaf149_p115_point_table.jpg sha256 083de3958ca9145e69c05a6d116490bc9909642ff94fd9ed0441aff3fdd49601, both fetched from the Wellcome item's IIIF endpoint). Quotation policy: quotes are verbatim early-modern English with exactly two restorations - long-s OCR artifacts normalized to 's', and planet/sign sigils that the OCR renders as junk glyphs restored in square brackets from context; residual numeric OCR doubts are recorded inside the affected rule rather than silently resolved. rendering_grade is verbatim_early_modern_english throughout; no translation was needed or performed, and no modern edited edition (Regulus 1985 or later regularizations) was consulted or quoted. Horary-specific doctrine (considerations before judgment, perfection of questions) is carried with domain 'other' and an explicit scope_note rather than being passed off as natal. Death-timing, lifespan (Hyleg/Alcocoden), and criminal/moralizing fate-claims in CA are deliberately NOT extracted; see the refusal list in defensibility_spec.md. Cross-references against the al-Qabisi Arabic pack (islamicate/al_qabisi_rule_manifest.json) are recorded per-rule in conflicts_with, including the void-of-course CONCORDANCE (both authors state the any-planet, remainder-of-sign definition), the orb-doctrine conflict (flat 6-degree application vs per-planet moieties), the reception divergence (one-directional qabul vs Lilly's mutual reception), and the Ptolemaic-vs-Egyptian terms conflict.

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

scope.chapter: Of severall Termes, Aspects, words of Art (CA pp. 105-109)

conditions.trigger: classifying any aspect between two planets

conclusion.quote: You must understand amongst these Aspects, the Quadrate Aspect is a signe of imperfect emnity; and that the Opposition is an aspect or argument of perfect hatred [...] The Sextill and Trine aspects are arguments of Love, Unity and Friendship; but the [Trine] is more forcible [...] Conjunctions are good or bad, as the Planets in [conjunction] are friends or enemies to one another.

quality.conjunction: good or bad according to the friendship of the two planets

conclusion.note: Opposition stated as 180 degrees, 'halfe the Circle'; conjunction as same degree and minute of a signe.

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: deciding whether an aspect is partill (exact) or platick (within orb-moiety)

conclusion.quote: Partill aspect is when two Planets are exactly so many degrees from each other as make a perfect aspect [...] A Platick Aspect is that which admits of the Orbs or Rayes of two Planets that signifie any matter: As if [Venus] be in the tenth degree of [Taurus], and [Saturn] in eighteen degrees of [Virgo], here [Venus] hath a Platick [trine], or is a Platick [trine] to [Saturn], because she is within the moity of both their Orbs; for the moity of [Saturn] his Rayes or Orbs is five, and of [Venus] 4, and the distance betwixt them and their perfect aspect is eight degrees.

predicate.partill: angular separation equals the perfect aspect exactly, by degree

conclusion.note: The worked example uses Saturn orb 10 (moiety 5) and Venus orb 8 (moiety 4), consistent with the first column of the p.107 orb table.

conflicts_with: islam.qabisi.ch3.application_orb_and_types (al-Qabisi states a flat 6-degree application orb; Lilly computes application/separation reach from the sum of the two planets' orb-moieties)

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: deciding whether one planet applies to another

conclusion.quote: Application of Planets is three severall wayes: First, when a Planet of more swift motion applies to one more slow and ponderous, they being both direct [...] Secondly, when both Planets are retrograde [...] this is an ill Application and an argument either suddenly perfecting, or breaking off the businesse [...] Thirdly, when a Planet is direct, and in fewer degrees, and a retrograde Planet being in more degrees of the Signe [...] this is an ill application.

application_modes.condition: swifter planet in fewer degrees moves toward the slower

application_modes.quality: ill; sudden perfection or breaking off

application_modes.condition: direct planet in fewer degrees, retrograde planet in more degrees closing on it

conflicts_with: islam.qabisi.ch3.application_orb_and_types (al-Qabisi defines application by the 6-degree rule and beholding signs; Lilly by motion classes and orb-moieties)

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: orienting an application, and naming an aspect dexter or sinister

conclusion.quote: the superiour Planets doe not apply to the inferiour (unlesse they be Retrograde), but the lighter to the more ponderous [...] this Aspect is called a Sinister [...] and it is an Aspect according to the succession of the Signes [...] and this is called a Dexter Aspect, and is against the order of Signes [...] Observe the dexter aspect is more forcible then the Sinister.

predicates.applier: the lighter (swifter) planet applies to the more ponderous; a superior planet applies to an inferior only when retrograde
predicates.sinister_aspect: cast in the order of the signs
predicates.dexter_aspect: cast against the order of the signs; more forcible than the sinister

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: deciding when two planets are separated, and when separation is complete

conclusion.quote: Separation, it is in the first place, when two Planets are departed but six minutes distance from each other [...] for every Planet that applies is allowed halfe his owne orbs and halfe the orbs of that Planet from whom he seperates: As if [Sun] and [Moon] be in any aspect, the [Moon] shall then be seperated from the [Sun], when she is fully distant from the [Sun] 7 degr. and 30 min. viz. half the orbs of the [Sun], and 6 degr. the moity of her owne orbes; in all 13 degr. and 30 minutes.

worked_examples.note: 'the halfe of [Jupiter] his orbe is 4 degr. 30 min. and the halfe of [Saturn] his orbe is 4 degr. 30 min. added together they make 9 whole degrees' - uses the 9-degree alternate orbs for both
uses Sun orb 15 (alternate column) and Moon orb 12

conclusion.timing_use: degrees remaining until complete separation are converted to weeks, days, months or years by sign quality (moveable hastens, common lengthens, fixed longest) - stated as horary timing, quoted for doctrine only

conflicts_with: islam.qabisi.ch3.application_orb_and_types (al-Qabisi: separation/inqita begins the moment the swifter passes the slower; Lilly: separation begins at 6 arc-minutes and completes only past the summed moieties)

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: a third planet completes a conjunction or aspect with the target before the applying planet can

conclusion.quote: Prohibition is when two Planets that signifie the effecting or bringing to conclusion any thing demanded, are applying to an Aspect, and before they can come to a true Aspect, another Planet interposeth either his body or aspect, so that thereby the matter propounded is hindered and retarded; this is called Prohibition.

variants.bodily_prohibition: a swifter third planet overtakes and conjoins the target first ('Conjunctionall or Bodily prohibition'); example: Mars 7 Aries applying to Saturn 12 Aries, Sun at 6 Aries overtakes Mars and conjoins Saturn first
variants.aspectal_prohibition: the interposing planet completes a sextile/square/trine/opposition ray to the target first; example: Mars 7 Aries, Saturn 13 Aries(?), Sun 5 Gemini passes his dexter sextile to Saturn before Mars' conjunction

conclusion.combustion_note: 'you must know that the combustion of any Planet is the greatest misfortune that can be' - stated inside the bodily-prohibition passage where the prohibiting body is the Sun

conflicts_with: islam.qabisi.ch3.frustration_variants (Lilly's prohibition corresponds to al-Qabisi's i'tirad/obstruction family; al-Qabisi splits the phenomenon into i'tirad, fawt and qat' al-nur, which Lilly does not distinguish)

conditions.trigger: the applying planet turns retrograde before perfecting the aspect

conclusion.quote: There's another manner of Prohibition, by some more properly called Refrenation; as thus, [Saturn] in 12 degr. of [Aries], [Mars] in 7 degr. here [Mars] hastens to a [conjunction] of [Saturn], but before he comes to the tenth or eleventh degree of [Aries] he becomes Retrograde, and by that meanes refraines to come to a [conjunction] of [Saturn] who still moves forward in the Signe; nothing signified by the former [conjunction] will ever be effected.

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

scope.chapter: terms of art (p. 111) and perfection chapter (p. 126)

conditions.trigger: a lighter planet separates from one significator and applies to the other

conclusion.quote: Translation of light and nature is, when a light Planet seperates from a more weighty one, and presently joynes to another more heavy [...] Its done also as well by any Aspect as by [conjunction].
conclusion.quote_perfection_form: some one Planet or other doth separate himselfe from one of the Significators, of whom he is received either by House, Triplicity or Terme, and then this Planet doth apply to the other Significator by [conjunction] or aspect, before he meeteth with the [conjunction] or aspect of any other Planet, he then translates the force, influence and vertue of the first Significator to the other.

predicates.form_book1: translator separates from heavier planet A, presently joins heavier planet B, by body or any aspect
predicates.form_perfection_chapter: adds two conditions: the translator must be RECEIVED by the planet it separates from (by house, triplicity or term), and must reach the second significator before meeting any other planet's ray

conclusion.internal_variation: Lilly's two statements differ: the Book 1 terms-of-art definition has no reception requirement; the perfection chapter adds it. Both are encoded; a consumer must choose and disclose.

conflicts_with: islam.qabisi.ch3.translation_and_collection_of_light (al-Qabisi's naql requires no reception; Lilly's perfection-chapter form requires the translator to be received by the first significator)

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: two significators that do not behold one another both aspect a heavier planet

conclusion.quote: Matters are also brought to perfection, when as the two principall Significators doe not behold one another, but both cast their severall Aspects to a more weighty Planet then themselves, and they both receive him in some of their essentiall dignities; then shall that Planet who thus collects both their Lights, bring the thing demanded to perfection [...] And this is called Collection.

conflicts_with: islam.qabisi.ch3.translation_and_collection_of_light (al-Qabisi's radd al-nur has no reception condition and adds a second form via a planet transferring between their degrees; Lilly requires double reception of the collector)

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: two significators stand in each other's essential dignities

conclusion.quote: Reception is when two Planets that are significators in any Question or matter, are in each others dignity; as [Sun] in [Aries], and [Mars] in [Leo]; here is reception of these two Planets by Houses; and certainly this is the strongest and best of all receptions. It may be by triplicity, terme or face, or any essentiall dignity.
conclusion.quote_effect: The use of this is much; for many times when as the effecting of a matter is denyed by the Aspects, or when the significators have no Aspect to each other, or when it seemes very doubtfull what is promised by [square] or [opposition] of the significators, yet if mutuall Reception happen betwixt the principall significators, the thing is brought to passe, and that without any great trouble, and suddenly to the content of both parties.

predicates.effect: perfects the matter even when aspects deny it, when there is no aspect, or when the aspect is square/opposition; without great trouble and to the content of both parties

worked_examples.condition: if the Question or Nativity be by day
worked_examples.note: planet sigils OCR-degraded in both witnesses; sign pair and by-day condition legible
each in the other's terms; degree numbers legible only partially (24 and 16), planets degraded - recorded, not restored

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: a planet stands in degrees where it has no essential dignity

conclusion.quote: A Planet is then said to be Peregrine, when he is in the degrees of any Signe wherein he hath no essentiall dignity: As [Saturn] in the tenth degree of [Aries], that Signe being not his House, Exaltation, or of his Triplicity, or he having in that degree either Terme or Face, he is then said to be Peregrine; had he been in 27, 28, &c. of [Aries], he could not be termed Peregrine, because then he is in his owne Terme.
conclusion.predicate: peregrine = no domicile, exaltation, triplicity, term or face at the exact degree occupied; degree-sensitive because terms and faces divide the sign
conclusion.horary_note: the significator of a thief is almost ever the peregrine planet in an angle or the second house - horary use, quoted for completeness

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: a planet separates and perfects no further aspect while in its sign

conclusion.quote: A Planet is voyd of course, when he is seperated from a Planet, nor doth forthwith, during his being in that Signe, apply to any other: This is most usually in the [Moon]; in judgements doe you carefully observe whether she be voyd of course yea or no; you shall seldome see a businesse goe handsomely forward when she is so.
conclusion.quote_exception: All manner of matters goe hardly on (except the principall significators be very strong) when the [Moon] is voyd of course; yet somewhat she performes if voyd of course, and be either in [Taurus], [Cancer], [Sagittarius] or [Pisces].

predicates.definition: separated from one planet and applying to no other for the remainder of its current sign
predicates.applies_to: any planet, but 'most usually' observed of the Moon
predicates.override: strong principal significators can carry a matter despite a void Moon

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: a planet is in the same sign as the Sun within 8 degrees 30 minutes

conclusion.quote: A Planet is said to be Combust of the [Sun], when in the same Signe where the [Sun] is in, he is not distant from the [Sun] eight degrees and thirty minutes, either before or after the [Sun] [...] you must observe a Planet is more afflicted when the [Sun] hastens to [conjunction] of him, then when the [Sun] recedes from him; in regard its the body of the [Sun] that doth afflict.

predicates.only_by_body: combustion can only be by personal conjunction in one sign, not by any aspect (stated p. 114)
predicates.sun_never_combust: all Planets may be in Combustion of the Sun, but he with none (p. 114)

conclusion.lilly_own_opinion: Lilly states he allows the moiety of the combust planet's OWN orb to show the time of combustion rather than the Sun's - 'by that rule [a planet] should not be combust before he is within four degrees and a half of the [Sun]. I know many are against this opinion.' Both the 8.30 rule and the own-moiety opinion are recorded; the 8.30 statement is the table rule.

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

conditions.trigger: classifying a planet as oriental or occidental of the Sun

conclusion.quote: [Saturn], [Jupiter] and [Mars] are Orientall of the [Sun], from the time of their [conjunction] with him, untill they come to his [opposition]: from whence untill they come to [conjunction] againe, they are said to be Occidentall: to be Oriental is no other thing then to rise before the [Sun]: to be Occidentall is to be seen [above] the Horizon, or to set after the [Sun] is downe.

predicates.superior_oriental: from conjunction with the Sun until his opposition
predicates.superior_occidental: from opposition until the next conjunction
predicates.mercury_venus: cannot make sextile/square/trine/opposition to the Sun; oriental when in fewer degrees of the Sun's sign or the preceding sign, occidental when in more degrees or the subsequent sign
predicates.moon: Orientall of the Sun from her opposition to her conjunction, and Occidentall from the conjunction to opposition

conclusion.ocr_note: the Venus elongation digits are degraded in both witnesses ('.' and garbled); 48 is the reading consistent with astronomy and with Lilly's other statements, recorded as an editorial restoration, and the Moon clause's first term reads 'from the time of her [opposition]' by the sense of the passage ('she farre exceeds the Sunne in swiftnesse').

rules.period: 1647 CE, London; English horary/natal synthesis of the medieval Latin tradition

scope.chapter: ch. VIII, Of the Planet Saturne, and his signification

conditions.trigger: delineating Saturn generally, keyed to its dignity state

conclusion.quote: He is a Diurnall Planet, Cold and Dry (being farre removed from the heat of the Sun) and moyst Vapours, Melancholick, Earthly, Masculine, the greater Infortune, author of Solitarinesse, Malevolent, &c.
conclusion.manners_well_dignified_quote: Then he is profound in Imagination, in his Acts severe, in words reserved, in speaking and giving very spare, in labour patient, in arguing or disputing grave, in obtaining the goods of this life studious and solicitous, in all manner of actions austere.
conclusion.manners_ill_dignified_quote: Then he is envious, covetous, jealous and mistrustfull, timorus, sordid, outwardly dissembling, sluggish, suspitious, stubborne, a contemner of women, a close lyar, malicious, murmuring, never contented, ever repining.

scope.chapter: ch. IX, Of the Planet Jupiter, and his signification

conditions.trigger: delineating Jupiter generally, keyed to its dignity state

conclusion.quote: He is a Diurnall, Masculine Planet, Temperately Hot and Moyst, Aiery, Sanguine, the greater Fortune, author of Temperance, Modesty, Sobriety, Justice.
conclusion.manners_well_dignified_quote: Then is he Magnanimous, Faithfull, Bashfull, Aspiring in an honourable way at high matters, in all his actions a Lover of faire Dealing, desiring to benefit all men, doing Glorious things, Honourable and Religious, of sweet and affable Conversation, wonderfully indulgent to his Wife and Children, reverencing Aged men, a great Reliever of the Poore, full of Charity and Godlinesse, Liberall, hating all Sordid actions, Just, Wise, Prudent, Thankfull, Vertuous.
conclusion.manners_ill_dignified_quote: When [Jupiter] is unfortunate, then he wastes his Patrimony, suffers every one to cozen him, is Hypocritically Religious, Tenacious, and stiffe in maintaining false Tenents in Religion; he is Ignorant, Carelesse, nothing Delightfull in the love of his Friends.
conclusion.orb_own_chapter: His Radiation or Orbe, is nine degrees before and after any his aspect
conclusion.planetary_hours: Thursday, and rules the first hour after [Sun] rise, and the eighth

scope.chapter: ch. X, Of the Planet Mars, and his severall significations

conditions.trigger: delineating Mars generally, keyed to its dignity state

conclusion.quote: He is a Masculine, Nocturnall Planet, in nature hot and dry, cholerick and fiery, the lesser Infortune, author of Quarrels, Strifes, Contentions.
conclusion.manners_well_dignified_quote: In feats of Warre and Courage invincible, scorning any should exceed him, subject to no Reason, Bold, Confident, Immoveable, Contentious, challenging all Honour to themselves, Valiant, lovers of Warre and things pertaining thereunto, hazarding himselfe to all Perils.
conclusion.manners_ill_dignified_quote: Then he is a Pratler without modesty or honesty, a lover of Slaughter and Quarrels, Murder, Theevery, a promoter of Sedition, Frayes and Commotions, an Highway-Theefe, as wavering as the Wind, a Traytor, of turbulent Spirit, Perjured, Obscene, Rash, Inhumane, neither fearing God or caring for man, Unthankful, Trecherous, Oppressors, Ravenous, Cheaters, Furious, Violent.

scope.chapter: ch. XI, Of the Sun, and his generall and particular significations

conditions.trigger: delineating Sun generally, keyed to its dignity state

conclusion.quote: He is naturally Hot, Dry, but more temperate then [Mars]; is a Masculine, Diurnall Planet, Equivalent, if well dignified, to a Fortune.
conclusion.benefic_malefic: equivalent to a fortune if well dignified
conclusion.manners_well_dignified_quote: Very faithfull, keeping their Promises with all punctuality, a kind of itching desire to Rule and Sway where he comes: Prudent, and of incomparable Judgment; of great Majesty and Statelinesse, Industrious to acquire Honour and a large Patrimony, yet as willingly departing therewith againe [...] Affable, Tractable, and very humane to all people.

scope.chapter: ch. XII, Of the Planet Venus and her severall significations and nature

conditions.trigger: delineating Venus generally, keyed to its dignity state

conclusion.quote: Shee is a Feminine Planet, temperately Cold and Moyst, Nocturnall, the lesser Fortune, author of Mirth and Jolity.
conclusion.manners_well_dignified_quote: Shee signifies a quiet man, not given to Law, Quarrel or Wrangling, not Vicious, Pleasant, Neat and Spruce, loving Mirth in his words and actions, cleanly in Apparel [...] prone to Venery, oft entangled in Love-matters, Musicall, delighting in Baths [...] a right vertuous Man or Woman.

scope.scope_note: HORARY-specific doctrine: these are gates on judging a horary question, not natal delineations. Domain set to 'other' accordingly; the Moon void-of-course clause is also cross-filed on lilly.ca1.void_of_course.

conditions.trigger: before delivering judgment on a horary figure

conclusion.quote: the Question then shall be taken for radicall, or fit to be judged, when as the Lord of the hour at the time of proposing the Question, and erecting the Figure, and the Lord of the Ascendant or first House, are of one Triplicity, or be one, or of the same nature.
considerations: radicality: lord of the hour agrees with lord of the ascendant (same planet, same triplicity, or same nature)
0-3 degrees ascending: judge not, unless the querent is very young and body/complexion agree
27-29 degrees ascending: judge not, unless the querent's age corresponds or the time is certain
Moon in late degrees of a sign, especially Gemini, Scorpio or Capricorn: not safe to judge
Moon in via combusta (last 15 degrees of Libra to first 15 degrees of Scorpio): not safe, 'as some say'
Moon void of course: matters go hardly on, except principal significators be very strong; somewhat performed in Taurus, Cancer, Sagittarius, Pisces
cusp of the 7th afflicted, or its lord retrograde/impedited (matter not of the 7th): the astrologer's judgment will give small content
Saturn in the ascendant, especially retrograde: the matter seldom comes to good; Saturn in the 7th corrupts the judgment of the astrologer
lord of the ascendant combust: neither question propounded will take, or the querent be regulated
lord of the 7th unfortunate, in fall, or in terms of the infortunes: the artist shall scarce give a solid judgment
testimonies of fortunes and infortunes equal: defer judgment

scope.chapter: ch. XXI, To know whether a thing demanded will be brought to perfection (CA pp. 124-126)
scope.scope_note: HORARY doctrine on how a matter perfects; encoded as 'other'. The aspect/reception machinery it exercises is the same machinery encoded in the natal-eligible rules above.

conditions.trigger: judging whether the thing demanded shall be accomplished

conclusion.quote: First, by Conjunction, when as therefore you find the Lord of the Ascendant, and Lord of that house which signifies the thing demanded, hastening to a [conjunction], and in the first house, or in any Angle, and the significators meet with no prohibition or refrenation before they come to perfect [conjunction]; you may then judge, that the thing sought after shall be brought to passe.

modes.conditions: significators hasten to conjunction in the first house or any angle, no prohibition or refranation; angles soonest, succedents slower, cadents with infinite loss of time
apply by partill sextile or trine out of good houses where essentially well dignified, no intervening malevolent aspect
apply by square, provided each planet has dignity in the degrees where it stands and applies out of proper and good houses, otherwise not
only with mutual reception by house out of friendly houses and the Moon translating; 'I have rarely seen any thing brought to perfection by this way'
significator of the thing demanded casually posited in the ascendant
